Container.Name: Lingshu-Home
Container.Overview: A self-hosted personal dashboard for links, browser bookmarks, nested categories and modular widgets, with a library for existing Markdown files and bookmark usage notes. Connect optional document directories to personal or shared spaces; originals stay in the directories you mount. Choose English or Simplified Chinese before the first start; the saved language also determines example bookmarks and cannot be switched later. SQLite is included; no external database is required. Open the WebUI to complete first-run setup. There is no default administrator password. Keep the /data mapping to preserve your database, saved icons, document metadata, recovery history and instance encryption keys. This template follows the latest published stable Linux amd64 image and runs as Unraid's appdata user (99:100). Document access is disabled and direct HTTPS is off until configured. Back up appdata and any mounted originals before upgrading; version 0.0.5 applies migration 008. See ReadMe for multiple directory mounts, optional TLS and upgrade steps. Exact version tags remain available for version pinning.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: lingshu home dashboard homepage bookmarks navigation startpage selfhosted markdown documents library
Container.Requires: Linux amd64 (x86-64). Persistent appdata storage writable by UID 99 and GID 100.

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Host HTTP port by default; HTTPS on this same port when both TLS file fields are configured. Keep container port 8080. For direct TLS, change the WebUI URL to https and use a certificate-covered hostname. Complete setup on your trusted LAN.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Database, saved icons, document metadata, recovery history and instance keys. Keep this mapping when recreating or upgrading. Existing directories must be writable by UID 99 and GID 100. Mount document originals separately.

Config.Name: Interface language
Config.Description: First-start language: en (English) or zh-CN (Simplified Chinese). Saved once; later field changes do not switch it. When upgrading from 0.0.1, keep the previous value, especially en for an English instance.

Config.Name: Allowed document roots
Config.Description: Optional JSON array of container paths, for example ["/documents/notes","/documents/projects"]. Keep [] to disable filesystem access. Add one Path mapping per existing host document directory, then connect it to a space in Home. See ReadMe; do not use /data, certificate directories or broad server roots.

Config.Name: TLS certificate file
Config.Description: Optional container path to a PEM certificate chain, for example /certs/fullchain.pem. Leave both TLS file fields empty for HTTP or HTTPS terminated by a reverse proxy. To enable direct HTTPS, add a read-only certificate-directory Path mapping, set both TLS fields and update the WebUI URL. See ReadMe.

Config.Name: TLS private key file
Config.Description: Optional container path to the matching PEM private key, for example /certs/privkey.pem. This is a file path, not the key contents. Requires the certificate field; both files must be readable by UID 99 and GID 100. Missing or invalid TLS files stop startup instead of falling back to HTTP.

Config.Name: HTTPS-only cookies
Config.Description: Keep false for direct HTTP. Set true when accessing Home through an HTTPS reverse proxy. Direct TLS configured with the certificate/key fields automatically uses Secure cookies. This cookie setting alone does not enable HTTPS.
